title: Infinite Product Measures and Kolmogorov Extension

items.title: Coordinate maps, finite-coordinate cylinders, and the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra
items.strategy: Fix an arbitrary index set and measurable coordinate spaces. Define the finite-coordinate projections and their inverse-image cylinders, then name the $\sigma$-algebra generated by those cylinders. State explicitly that this is the product $\sigma$-algebra already defined in the library, rather than a second competing product construction.

items.title: Finite-coordinate cylinders form a $\pi$-system
items.strategy: Pull two cylinders back to the finite union of their coordinate sets and intersect their finite-dimensional measurable bases. This handles overlapping and disjoint coordinate supports uniformly.

items.title: Finite-coordinate cylinder sets form an algebra
items.strategy: At the finite union of all coordinates involved, complements and finite unions are inverse images of the corresponding finite-dimensional measurable sets. Keep this algebra distinct from the smaller rectangle-cylinder $\pi$-system.

items.title: A consistent family of finite-dimensional distributions
items.strategy: For every finite coordinate set give a probability law on its finite product. Require compatibility under every coordinate projection and under re-ordering, so the notation does not accidentally depend on a chosen enumeration of a finite set.

items.title: Consistent finite-dimensional laws define a well-defined finitely additive cylinder premeasure
items.strategy: Represent a cylinder on the union of all coordinates used by competing presentations. Projection consistency proves equality of assigned values; finite additivity follows after lifting a finite disjoint decomposition to one finite-dimensional product.

items.title: The countable-product cylinder premeasure is countably additive
items.strategy: For a countable sequence of arbitrary probability spaces, prove continuity at the empty set on the cylinder algebra by the finite-stage section argument used in Kajino. Combine it with finite additivity to obtain the premeasure condition; no Polish or compactness assumption is introduced here.

items.title: Countable products of arbitrary probability spaces
items.strategy: Apply Carathéodory extension to the countably additive cylinder premeasure and use the cylinder $\pi$-system for uniqueness. State only the product-marginal case over arbitrary measurable spaces; the later theorem is the genuinely stronger arbitrary-index extension from compatible finite-dimensional laws.

items.title: Coordinate random elements of a countable product are independent
items.strategy: Evaluate each finite-coordinate rectangle under the product measure and compare with the defining finite-family criterion for independence. Record the coordinate law at the same time for use in the copies corollary.

items.title: Countably many independent copies of a prescribed law exist
items.strategy: Specialize the countable product to a constant sequence of one measurable probability space and take the coordinate maps. This establishes existence, rather than presupposing a source probability space rich enough to contain the copies.

items.title: Stochastic processes and their finite-dimensional distributions
items.strategy: Define an indexed family of random elements with possibly varying state spaces and define its ordered finite-dimensional laws through finite coordinate projections. Make clear that the full family, not merely its one-dimensional marginals, is the relevant data.

items.title: Process law, modification, and indistinguishability
items.strategy: Separate equality of all finite-dimensional laws, a modification (equality almost surely at each fixed time), and indistinguishability (one null set works for all times). Require measurable diagonals for the fixed-time equality formulation, and phrase indistinguishability by a null exceptional set rather than an unjustified uncountable intersection.

items.title: Standard Borel spaces
items.strategy: Define a standard Borel measurable space as one measurably isomorphic to the Borel measurable space of a Polish space. Retain the measurable-space structure, not a chosen topology, as the datum.

items.title: Finite products of standard Borel spaces are standard Borel
items.strategy: Transport the finite products through Polish presentations and use the finite-product Polish construction. Verify that the transported Borel $\sigma$-algebra agrees with the finite product $\sigma$-algebra.

items.title: Borel probability measures on Polish spaces are inner regular
items.strategy: Use the standard tightness construction for a finite Borel measure on a complete separable metric space: choose compact approximants with summable losses and pass to their compact intersection. State the compact-set approximation precisely, since it is the compactness input for arbitrary-index extension.

items.title: Kolmogorov extension for arbitrary families of standard Borel coordinate spaces
items.strategy: Use consistency to define a finitely additive cylinder law. Approximate the finite-dimensional cylinder bases from inside by compact sets, apply the compact finite-intersection argument in the arbitrary product, obtain continuity at the empty set, and extend by Carathéodory. Prove uniqueness only on the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra by the cylinder $\pi$-system. The compact-product step follows the design's BPI/ultrafilter route; the current library Tychonoff item is an AC-scoped seam recorded in the notes.

items.title: Arbitrary products of standard Borel probability spaces
items.strategy: Take the finite-dimensional laws to be finite products of the prescribed coordinate laws, verify their projection consistency, and invoke Kolmogorov extension. The conclusion is a measure on the cylinder/product $\sigma$-algebra, not on the full power set of the path space.

items.title: The canonical coordinate process realizes consistent finite-dimensional laws
items.strategy: Equip the product space with the extension measure and use its coordinate projections as the process. Read the requested finite-dimensional distribution directly from the defining cylinder values.

items.title: Finite-dimensional distributions determine a process law on the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra
items.strategy: The finite-dimensional laws agree exactly on cylinder sets. Apply the $\pi$-$\lambda$ uniqueness argument to conclude equality on the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra, and do not claim equality for nonmeasurable subsets or a larger unspecified $\sigma$-algebra.

items.title: Cylinder-measurable events depend on only countably many coordinates
items.strategy: Show that the events determined by some countable coordinate subset form a $\sigma$-algebra containing every finite-coordinate cylinder. Generated-$\sigma$ minimality then gives the claim for every cylinder-measurable event.

items.title: The cylinder $\sigma$-algebra need not be the full path-space power set
items.strategy: Record the measurable-space boundary of every preceding extension theorem and point ahead to the countable-coordinate lemma and the nonmeasurable-path-functional counterexample. Do not turn this boundary warning into an unsupported cardinality classification.

items.title: State-space and index-set boundaries of the two extension routes
items.strategy: Contrast the arbitrary-measurable-space countable product theorem with the arbitrary-index standard-Borel extension theorem. State that compatible finite-dimensional laws alone are not being extended here outside standard Borel coordinates, and direct kernel-based constructions to the later Markov-chain page.

title: Infinite Product Measures and Kolmogorov Extension — Examples

items.title: The infinite fair-coin-toss space
items.strategy: Apply the countable product theorem to $\{0,1\}$ with the fair Bernoulli law. Calculate one finite cylinder probability and identify the coordinate tosses as independent.

items.title: An i.i.d. sequence with a prescribed law
items.strategy: Instantiate the independent-copies corollary for a supplied probability law and verify the common marginal and finite-family independence in the canonical construction.

items.title: Independent but non-identically distributed coordinates
items.strategy: Use a countable product with alternating or otherwise unequal Bernoulli parameters. Check independence from the product theorem and exhibit two coordinates with different one-dimensional laws.

items.title: A canonical random walk from product increments
items.strategy: Take independent $\{-1,1\}$-valued coordinate increments on the product space and define partial sums. Verify the finite-dimensional increment law and distinguish the process coordinates from the increment coordinates.

items.title: An uncountable Bernoulli coordinate process
items.strategy: For an arbitrary uncountable index set, prescribe fair Bernoulli finite-dimensional product laws and apply the standard-Borel Kolmogorov theorem. Emphasize that the resulting measure is on the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra.

items.title: A modification need not be indistinguishable
items.strategy: On a space carrying a uniform random time $U$, let $X_t=0$ and set $Y_t=1$ only when $t=U$. Each fixed-time equality fails on a null event, whereas no single null set removes the discrepancy at the random time. Check the measurable-diagonal convention from the definition.

items.title: One-dimensional marginals alone do not specify a joint law
items.strategy: Compare equal fair bits with two independent fair bits. Their one-dimensional marginals agree, but the two-dimensional probability of equality differs, so the required data are full compatible finite-dimensional distributions.

items.title: A noncylinder path functional may fail to be measurable
items.strategy: For an uncountable Bernoulli path space, choose an uncountable coordinate-sensitive event such as the set of paths with uncountably many ones. The countable-coordinate lemma shows it is not cylinder-measurable, so its indicator is not a random variable for the canonical cylinder-space construction.
